name: Josh Smead
bio: Josh Smead is a licensed architect and small-business owner from Liberty, Missouri. He won the 2026 Democratic primary for Missouri's 6th Congressional District and frames his campaign around project-management accountability.

platform.point: Reverse tax cuts for the wealthy and end broad, unpredictable tariffs that raise prices on imports.
Back a universal healthcare system with a focus on rural access and funding for struggling hospitals.
Oppose school vouchers, raise public school funding, and fund universal pre-K and school meals.
Replace ICE with humane legal immigration enforcement housed outside DHS and bar military use in deportations.
Support the Grain Belt Express, reverse EPA budget cuts and plan long term for climate change.
Protect family farms from rising costs and support farmers' right to repair equipment.

economy.evidence: Calls for reversing tax cuts for wealthy individuals and ending sweeping tariffs.

welfare.evidence: Supports a universal healthcare system and universal pre-K and school meals.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and transgender rights, while backing background checks and registration of 3D-printed guns.

security.evidence: Opposes government gathering of personal data and military use for arrests and deportations.

immigration.evidence: Proposes eliminating ICE and protecting immigrants targeted by current enforcement.

energy.evidence: Wants EPA cuts reversed, fossil-fuel deregulation stopped and long-term climate planning.

education.evidence: Opposes vouchers that divert public school money and wants more federal and state school funding.

faith.evidence: Wants religion kept out of public schools while also pledging to protect religious freedom.

notes: Several scores filled from the campaign's plan page, which is more detailed than the earlier basis.

name: Andy Maidment
current_role: Retired Army officer and IT security professional
bio: Andy Maidment is a retired U.S. Army officer who works in information technology security. He is the Libertarian nominee for Missouri's 6th Congressional District in 2026.
notes: No campaign website or issue statements could be located; background is from the Wikipedia election page only.

name: Eric Burlison
bio: Eric Burlison has represented Missouri's 7th Congressional District since 2023 and is a member of the House Freedom Caucus. He previously served in the Missouri House (2009-2016) and Missouri Senate (2019-2023) and worked as a software engineer and business analyst. Born in Springfield, he holds a philosophy degree and an MBA from Missouri State University.

platform.point: Opposes state and local bans on natural gas and promotes domestic fossil-fuel production.
Introduced the Great American Healthcare Act (H.R. 8324).
Co-sponsored a bill barring federal funds for license plate readers and biometric surveillance cameras.
Chairs the Oversight subcommittee on economic growth, energy policy and regulatory affairs, focused on cutting regulation.
Introduced a bill in 2025 recognizing legal personhood from conception.

economy.evidence: Freedom Caucus member who chairs a subcommittee focused on regulatory rollback.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicaid cuts and adding work requirements.

liberty.evidence: Introduced a personhood-at-conception bill (abortion) while sponsoring constitutional carry and backing absolute gun rights (guns).

security.evidence: Co-sponsored legislation to bar federal funding for license plate readers and biometric surveillance cameras.

foreign.evidence: Voted in 2023 for withdrawing U.S. troops from Syria and against a 2024 resolution on Ukrainian children.

energy.evidence: Opposes natural gas bans and advocates for fossil-fuel producers.

tech.evidence: One of two House members to vote against the Take It Down Act.

education.evidence: Supported expanding charter schools and strongly favors school vouchers.

notes: Supported aid to Israel after the 2023 Hamas attack, which tempers the low foreign score. No sourced immigration stance was found, so that domain is unscored.

name: Missi Hesketh
current_role: Teacher and former Mayor of Forsyth
bio: Missi Hesketh is a teacher and former mayor of Forsyth, Missouri. She was the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 7th Congressional District in 2024 and is the party's nominee again in 2026.

platform.point: Close tax loopholes for billionaires, protect Social Security, add paid family leave and ban junk fees.
Offer Medicare to anyone who wants it, stabilize rural hospitals and expand Medicare drug price negotiation.
Invest in rural schools and workforce training and raise teacher pay.
Pass right-to-repair, reform crop insurance and block foreign adversaries from buying U.S. farmland.
Ban congressional stock trading, set term limits, audit the Pentagon and end Citizens United.

economy.evidence: Proposes closing billionaire tax loopholes, curbing grocery price gouging and banning junk fees.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for all who want it and paid family and medical leave.

tech.evidence: Calls for comprehensive children's data privacy and opposes AI data centers.

education.evidence: Prioritises investment in rural public education and higher teacher pay.

notes: Her site lists 'politicians out of your doctor's office' and 'safe gun ownership' without detail, so liberty was left unscored.

name: Kevin Craig
bio: Kevin Craig is the Libertarian nominee for Missouri's 7th Congressional District and is based in Powersite, Missouri. He holds a law degree and describes himself as a Christian libertarian and pacifist.

platform.point: Cut federal spending by trillions and abolish the Education Department, IRS and HHS.
Opposes the federal income tax.
Opposes military intervention, foreign aid and overseas bases in favor of peaceful trade with all nations.
Would re-legalize drugs, arguing prohibition does more harm than good.
Favors private charity over federal programs such as Social Security and Medicare.

economy.evidence: Opposes income taxation and wants most federal programs abolished.

welfare.evidence: Favors private charity in place of Social Security and Medicare.

liberty.evidence: Would re-legalize drugs (drugs) but opposes abortion (abortion).

foreign.evidence: Pacifist who opposes intervention, foreign aid and overseas bases.

education.evidence: Would abolish the Education Department and favors school choice and private Christian schooling.

faith.evidence: Rejects modern church-state separation doctrine and promotes Christian influence in government, though not by coercion.

notes: Positions come from his long-running personal campaign site; its abortion stance is stated briefly.

name: Jason Smith
bio: Jason Smith has represented Missouri's 8th Congressional District since a 2013 special election and has chaired the House Ways and Means Committee since 2023. He served in the Missouri House from 2005 to 2013 and previously worked in real estate. He holds degrees from the University of Missouri and Oklahoma City University School of Law.

platform.point: Promotes tax cuts so people keep more of their paychecks, including relief for farmers and small businesses.
Aims to limit federal interference in Missouri and favor state and local control.
Backs President Trump's border security push and immigration enforcement agencies.
Lists support for farms and rural producers as a core priority.
Pledges that government will respect, not interfere with, family and faith values.

economy.evidence: Supported the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and champions further tax cuts as Ways and Means chair.

welfare.evidence: Calls for repealing the ACA and requiring photo ID to use food stamps.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion (abortion) while voting for concealed carry reciprocity (guns) and opposing the same-sex marriage ruling (LGBTQ).

security.evidence: Supported ending bulk data collection under the PATRIOT Act and opposes warrantless phone surveillance.

immigration.evidence: Backs Trump's border enforcement, though he has supported higher high-skill and family visa caps.

energy.evidence: Supports offshore oil and gas drilling and state leasing of federal lands for extraction.

education.evidence: Backs vouchers and the A-PLUS state flexibility program.

faith.evidence: Backs faith-based objections to same-sex marriage services and a biblical view of marriage.

name: Christopher Reichard
bio: Christopher Reichard is an Army veteran of Operation Iraqi Freedom from Arnold, Missouri, and a second-generation member of IBEW Local 1. He won the 2026 Democratic primary for Missouri's 8th Congressional District.

platform.point: Pass the PRO Act to protect organizing rights and strengthen unions.
Pass the Major Richard Star Act so combat-injured veterans get full benefits.
Keep the U.S. out of another prolonged war and support the Full Cost of War Act.
End Citizens United and remove dark money from elections; refuses corporate PAC money.
Support the Equality Act and the REPAIR Act.

economy.evidence: Supports the PRO Act and stronger unions.

foreign.evidence: Wants to avoid another forever war and backs the Full Cost of War Act.

notes: Wikipedia describes him as a construction worker; the liberty score rests on a single issue.

name: Rebecca Sharpe Lombard
bio: Rebecca Sharpe Lombard is the Libertarian nominee for Missouri's 8th Congressional District in 2026.
notes: No campaign website, biography or issue statements could be located.

name: Aaron Flint
bio: Aaron Flint has hosted a statewide Montana radio program for 17 years and is a military veteran who served in Iraq and Afghanistan. He won the 2026 Republican primary for Montana's 1st Congressional District.

platform.point: Ban Wall Street purchases of single-family homes and back federally backed mortgages for first responders and teachers.
Make permanent the tax breaks on tips, overtime and Social Security.
Expand timber harvests, cut business regulation and end the Roadless Rule.
Keep federal public lands from being sold and expand access infrastructure.
No pay for Congress without a budget, a balanced budget amendment and a stock trading ban.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting business regulations and permanent tax breaks.

immigration.evidence: Campaign homepage calls for a secure border and deporting criminals.

foreign.evidence: Opposes limits on presidential war powers and supports the administration's Iran approach, while criticizing forever wars.

energy.evidence: Lists unleashing American energy dominance among his priorities and backs expanded timber harvests.

notes: Border and energy stances come from the campaign homepage; its gun-rights language appears only in an endorsement quote, so liberty was not scored.

name: Sam Forstag
bio: Sam Forstag spent eight years as a wildland firefighter, including four as a smokejumper, and in 2025 became vice president of NFFE Local 60, representing Forest Service workers. Born in Ohio and raised largely in Portland, Oregon, he moved to Montana in 2012 and studied at the University of Montana. He has also worked as an organizer for the ACLU of Montana and as a lobbyist.

platform.point: Raise the corporate rate to 35%, set a 30% minimum tax on millionaires and tax billion-dollar fortunes.
Offer a Medicare option to all, free for working people, and expand it to dental, vision and hearing.
Fund community land trusts, encourage zoning reform and ban hedge-fund purchases of homes.
Provide universal free childcare and universal pre-K, and keep public money in public schools.
Impose strict federal AI oversight and regulate social media algorithms that target children.
Raise the federal minimum wage to $15 indexed to inflation and pass the PRO Act.

economy.evidence: Proposes a 35% corporate rate, a millionaire minimum tax, a billionaire wealth tax and a $15 minimum wage.

welfare.evidence: Supports a Medicare option for all and universal free childcare.

liberty.evidence: Would codify Roe v. Wade (abortion) and pledges to defend gun rights with voluntary safe-storage programs (guns).

security.evidence: Wants judicial warrants for immigration searches, facial recognition limits and bans on masked enforcement.

immigration.evidence: Backs comprehensive reform with a path to citizenship and more accountability for immigration agents.

tech.evidence: Calls for strict federal AI oversight, data opt-outs and regulation of social media algorithms aimed at kids.

education.evidence: Wants public dollars kept in public schools, federal teacher-pay matching grants and universal pre-K.

name: Nick Sheedy
bio: Nick Sheedy is the Libertarian nominee for Montana's 1st Congressional District in 2026. He presents his independence from both major parties as a way to influence close votes in Congress.

platform.point: Strengthen the War Powers Resolution so presidents need congressional authorization for military action.
Eliminate the Federal Reserve and return control of currency to Congress.
Improve access mainly by reducing regulatory burdens on providers, while keeping VA facilities.
Pass federal legislation to overturn Citizens United, modeled on Montana's campaign finance rules.
Limit federal deployment of the National Guard to constitutional purposes.

economy.evidence: Would eliminate the Federal Reserve and reduce regulation.

welfare.evidence: Prefers lowering healthcare regulation over expanded federal programs.

foreign.evidence: Would require congressional authorization before presidential military action.

notes: No campaign website or biographical details were found.

name: Kimberly Persico
bio: Kimberly Persico, of Hot Springs, Montana, previously worked as an analytical chemist and math instructor in Wisconsin. In Montana she has worked in ranching, at a stockyard and veterinary clinic, and as a school paraprofessional, and founded an environmental consulting firm serving mining operations. She is running as a self-described conservative independent.

platform.point: Supports congressional term limits and the Transparent Election Initiative to limit election spending.
Wants to address the federal fiscal imbalance.
Put ordinary people ahead of large corporations and billionaires.
Protect public lands and support agriculture.

notes: The campaign site cited on Wikipedia (keepingamericaspromise.com) currently redirects to a WordPress error page. Her stated themes are too general to score.
